title: Configured Operation
event: The store's operation reconfigures itself: mezzanine service shutters slide into new slots, self-checkout kiosks rotate on their bases to form aligned lanes, and hundreds of shopping carts lock together into a single-file river that slowly rolls toward the main entrance.
consequence: A single-file river of locked shopping carts moves down the central aisle toward the entrance.
nextHook: the cart-river meets the deli conveyors
stillPrompt: Interior shot of the Kaufhaus main floor, recognizable high ceilings, glass mezzanine and central escalators. The mezzanine shutters are partially closed into new vertical ribs, banks of self-checkout kiosks have rotated so screens form continuous surfacing, and dozens of shopping carts have mechanically latched into a single-file chain slowly rolling down the central aisle toward the entrance. Overhead fluorescent light pools and reflections in the polished floor emphasize the newly ordered circulation. No visible text or logos, no monster.
videoPrompt: Five-second slow push: shutters slide fully into place, kiosks rotate smoothly into alignment, the chained carts begin to roll as a slow mechanical river, echoes and small clacks as metal links click. Camera stabilizes as the river of carts advances under the mezzanine lights, revealing the reconfigured circulation.
cameraCue: After the carts lock and begin rolling, camera pulls back and rises slightly to reveal the full length of the cart river and the reoriented kiosks.

title: Butchered Logistics
event: Refrigerated deli counters and conveyor lines begin to feed into the cart-river: wrapped trays and packages shift, small unlabelled slabs of raw, wet tissue-like material detach from display racks and tumble onto a moving conveyor, arranging into precise stacks that mirror the cart chain's rhythm.
consequence: A neat pile of unlabelled, fleshy slabs is amassed on a conveyor that will be carried toward the cart river.
nextHook: the conveyor carries stamped slabs onto the tiled floor
stillPrompt: Close, tactile interior of the Kaufhaus deli and conveyor junction. Cold glass cases fog, trays of indistinct, raw flesh-like slabs glisten under the display lamps; a conveyor takes several small slabs and stacks them into ordered piles as condensation beads and tiny drips fall to the stainless surface. The arrangement of stacks matches the rhythm of the cart river beyond a glass partition. No readable labels, no logos, no monster.
videoPrompt: Two-second micro-shot: conveyor belt cycles, slabs slide and nest into stacks, droplets fall and evaporate; the glass case exhales a soft mist. The conveyor hum matches a muffled metallic clack from the cart river beyond, linking the two systems.
cameraCue: After the last slab drops into place, camera tilts up slightly to show the conveyor's piles lined up toward the partition where the cart river waits.

title: Stamped Path
event: Heavy, stencil-like stamps begin to press onto the polished floor tiles: wet, dark marks in unfamiliar glyphic shapes are hammered in a repeating sequence, creating a continuous path of stamped motifs that leads from the conveyor across the main hall toward the far escalator.
consequence: A dark, wet path of repeated stamped motifs runs across the floor, visually directing circulation toward the far escalator.
nextHook: the public organizes itself to follow the stamped path
stillPrompt: Overhead, the Kaufhaus tile floor as a mechanical stamp descends in sequence, leaving a row of wet, dark glyph-like impressions that form a continuous walking path from the deli conveyor to the distant escalator. The stamps look like hazard-style pictorial marks (no readable text) and the wet traces reflect the upper light banks. The conveyor and cart river are visible at the frame edge but no people or monster are present.
videoPrompt: Three-second overhead pan as each stamp descends and the wet glyph darkens, a small ripple of condensation spreading outward before beginning to dry. The stamped line advances steadily across the tiles toward the escalator.
cameraCue: After the final stamp hits and the wet path darkens, camera dollies forward low and follows the stamped motifs toward the escalator.

title: The Public Forms
event: Shoppers and staff respond to the stamped path: small groups step only onto the stamped tiles and fall into a precise procession that follows the path; others cluster to the sides, mimicking the pattern, forming a slow-moving human procession that advances toward the far escalator and blocks the central access.
consequence: A dense, synchronized procession of people is now moving along the stamped path, congesting the approach to the escalator.
nextHook: the procession reaches the end of the path and confronts something at its terminus
stillPrompt: Mid-level view of the Kaufhaus atrium: dozens of shoppers and employees step deliberately onto the stamped tiles and fall into a slow, synchronized procession that follows the dark path across the floor toward the far escalator. People carry shopping bags and small parcels, they avoid untamped tiles as though guided by the trace; faces are intent, not panicked. No monster is visible.
videoPrompt: Two-second steady push as the procession advances in slow, rhythmic steps; murmur and shoe-on-tile percussion sync with the wet stamps' fading drip. The human column compresses as it approaches the escalator.
cameraCue: After the procession coheres, camera moves to a low shoulder-height behind the crowd to emphasize the blocked approach to the escalator.

title: Rupture at the Terminus
event: At the end of the stamped path a weathered, practical sculpture—an assembled hulking figure of pitted metal, patched fabric and dented plates—stands rooted to the floor, already integrated into the scene. The procession collides with it: carts jam against its base, a shopping cart is crushed and trapped under one limb, handrails bend. The crowd presses in, security barriers clang; overhead lights vibrate.
consequence: A crushed shopping cart jammed beneath the weathered sculpture and a bent metal handrail remain as visible damage at the terminus.
nextHook: store operations convert the damage into merchandise and commerce
stillPrompt: Location-reanchored interior of the Kaufhaus atrium showing, at the end of the stamped path, a weathered practical sculpture already in place: a hulking assemblage of pitted metal, stitched fabric and dented plates standing like an artifact on the tile. Its surface is scarred and aged; a crushed shopping cart is wedged under a limb and a bent handrail lies nearby. A dense procession of people presses up against it; some reach, some recoil. Overhead lights rattle slightly; dust motes move in the shafts. The sculpture is presented as a physical, filmed object in the space. No readable text or logos.
videoPrompt: Two-second shot: subtle breathing micro-movement of the practical sculpture (a minimal settle and exhale of fabric and plate), the crowd shuffles and presses, a security barrier swings and clangs, and the overhead luminaires flicker in sympathy. The sculpture does not appear or materialize during the shot—it is present at the start.
cameraCue: After the crowd presses in and the cart crushes, camera holds on a waist-high vantage to frame the sculpture, the crushed cart under its limb, and the bent handrail as the scene's visible rupture.

title: Commercial Absorption
event: The Kaufhaus reorganizes the rupture into commerce: staff quickly remove minor debris and set up a temporary fold-out stall using crushed cart metal as display racks; small polished, weathered miniatures (replicas of the sculpture's pitted plate and stitched fabric fragments) are placed in clear acrylic plinths and offered on a folding table. Customers line up and exchange coins for the salvaged mementos.
consequence: A table of small, weathered replicas—salvaged fragments cast and displayed—sits on a folding stall made from crushed cart metal; shoppers carry the small replicas away.
nextHook: the commercial circulation folds the incident into everyday consumption (conflict remains open)
stillPrompt: Close interior of the Kaufhaus near the damaged terminus: a temporary fold-out stall built from bent cart metal and crate wood displays small, weathered replicas—polished fragments echoing the sculpture's plates and stitched fabric—set in clear plinths. Staff hand items to waiting shoppers; small bundles and coins exchange hands. The crushed cart and bent handrail are visible at frame edge, now repurposed as part of the display structure. No monster is visible.
videoPrompt: Two-second action: hands exchange a small weathered replica, a clerk slides a plinth across the table, and a shopper walks away clutching the object. The lighting is steady, with a distant hum from floor-cleaning machinery and the faint motion of the cart-river visible beyond.
cameraCue: After a small replica is handed over, camera closes on the customer's hands clutching it, then tilts to include the crushed cart repurposed as display support at the stall's edge.
